subject: Renewal: reserved pool bump & revised pricing (16→32 GPUs) — proposal for NovaCorp
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@novacorp.com>, procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: reserved pool bump & revised pricing (16→32 GPUs) — proposal for NovaCorp

Hi Ben / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I pulled together two renewal options to cover NovaCorp's growth over the next 12 months. Summary:

- Current: 16 reserved GPUs (monthly reserved hours).
- Proposal A (recommended): Increase to 32 reserved GPUs, 12-month commit, 10% uplift on baseline monthly hours to allow burst traffic.
- Pricing: Revised reserved-rate of $1.45/hr/GPU (down from $1.90/hr under one-off hourly), applied to committed hours; overage billed at on-demand rate with a 20% blended cap.
- Throughput guarantee: 99th-percentile token latency SLO within 1.3x of current baseline for standard prompt profiles; included automatic fallback to compatible quantized variant if we detect sustained capacity pressure.

Attached: NovaCorp_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (line-item pricing, committed-hours examples, and sample SLA).

If procurement prefers a balance-sheet friendly option we can also provide a prepay (3% incremental discount for annual prepayment).

Next steps: if this looks reasonable, I can route an amended order form + SLA for signature and loop in finance/legal for any redlines. Keen to finalize before the end of May to lock pricing.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@novacorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>, legal <legal@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: reserved pool bump & revised pricing (16→32 GPUs) — proposal for NovaCorp

Olga,

Thanks — appreciate the clear options. A few things from our side:

1) Cost sensitivity: moving to 32 GPUs is fine, but we need a better sting on the committed per-hour price. $1.45/hr is an improvement but currently puts our projected monthly bill 28% higher than the budget target.
2) SLO clarity: the 99th percentile language is ok, but we need an explicit credit formula if SLOs are missed (example credit as % of monthly invoice).
3) Overage predictability: rather than a blended cap we prefer a hard cap on overage hours per month (e.g., 15% of committed hours) after which you automatically enable spot-burst capacity at fixed surcharge.

Can your team provide a counter that tightens committed pricing and adds a formal SLO credit? We aim to present to Finance & CTO next Tuesday.

—Ben
Ben Wallace
Director of AI Infrastructure, NovaCorp
ben.wallace@novacorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0124

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: reserved pool bump & revised pricing (16→32 GPUs) — quick pricing ask

Marissa / Marcus — forwarding Ben's note. He pushed back on committed per-hour and wants explicit SLO credits + a hard overage cap.

Options I'm thinking:
- Option 1 (Aggressive discount): Move to $1.25/hr/GPU for committed hours if NovaCorp pre-pays annually (3.5% delta vs our original). Include SLO credit: 5% credit of monthly committed invoice if 99th latency exceeds target more than twice in a month. Hard cap: 15% overage hours/month, thereafter auto-burst at +30% surcharge.
- Option 2 (Balanced): $1.35/hr with month-to-month billing, same SLO credit but higher surcharge for burst (+45%).

I need sign-off from finance on Option 1 profitability. Marcus — can you confirm the margin math and whether we can approve the prepay discount + SLO credit? Also, if legal wants a stricter credit formula we'll need to loop them.

If we can push Option 1 I can get the amended order form and SLA over with a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Olga

Onward —
Olga Petrov
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@novacorp.com>, procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-06T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal: reserved pool bump & revised pricing (16→32 GPUs) — proposal for NovaCorp

Ben — thanks for the note and for outlining NovaCorp's constraints. After internal alignment, here's a revised offer that addresses your asks: 

Revised offer (final):
- Capacity: 32 reserved GPUs, 12-month term.
- Committed rate: $1.28/hr/GPU for committed hours (applies to baseline committed hours per month).
- Prepay option: 3.0% discount off committed invoice if NovaCorp elects annual prepayment.
- Overage policy: Soft overage cap at 15% of committed hours/month. If usage exceeds 15% in a billing month, auto-burst will be enabled at a fixed surcharge of +30% on the committed hourly rate for excess hours.
- SLO & credits: 99th-percentile latency SLO; if SLO target is missed more than twice in a calendar month, NovaCorp receives a 6% credit on that month's committed portion of the invoice.
- Throughput guarantee: We will commit to throughput testing during onboarding and include a baseline performance profile in the SLA.

Attachments: Amended_Order_Form.docx (order summary + signature block), Throughput_SLA.pdf (detailed SLOs and credit calculation). DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/link/ABC123-NOVACORP

If this is acceptable I'll send the DocuSign and loop in legal for the SLA redlines. Targeting a May 20 effective date so we can schedule onboarding and capacity migration in June.

Awaiting confirmation.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
